text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's constitutional tribunal ruled in favour of the tax inspectors' right to information about the taxpayer's bank account when administrative proceedings against him or her are underway. However, the tax office must not publish information on the level of taxes paid or overdue.

- U.S. President Bill Clinton plans to visit Poland around July 10, senior aid to the Polish President, Marek Siwiec, said. A group of the U.S. officials has already arrived in Warsaw to prepare the visit.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The general shareholders meeting of the Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank turned down the board's proposal for an up to 100 million zlotys share issue and appointed Grzegorz Wojtowicz as the bank's new president.
- Poland's current account and trade deficit as well as credit growth are too high, the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) reresentative to Poland said.

- Poland's Finance Minister Marek Belka has confirmed plans to limit the 1998 budget deficit to less than two percent of the gross domestic product (GDP). According to Belka, the $16 billion current account deficit envisaged by the central bank for 1998 will not hurt the economy.
- A barter house has been set up in Rzeszow, south-eastern Poland, to clear trade between companies from Poland, Hungary, Ukraine and Slovakia.
- The Polski Monopol Loteryjny and the Totalizator Sportowy state-owned lotteries will be changed into joint stock companies fully-owned by the treasury, the cabinet decided on Tuesday.
- Poland's GDP grew by 6.1 percent in 1996 and not by 6.0 percent as reported earlier, according to the corrected data published by the Central Statistical Office (GUS).
- The KGHM copper giant now under privatisation will not be able to cut production costs to $1,450 per tonne before 2005, a report by Britain's BZW investment bank said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Warsaw telephone lines and exchanges controlled by the Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecoms monopolist broke down on Tuesday due to callers' overload, TPSA said.

- The PZU SA, Poland's biggest insurance firm collected gross premiums worth 2.049 billion zlotys in the first quarter of 1997 and paid out 618 million zlotys in damages. The firm's net profit in the period was 205 million zlotys, showing significant growth compared with a net loss of 57 million zlotys in the first quarter of 1996.
PARKIET
- The listed Indykpol poultry processor will pay out 927,350 zlotys out of the 1996 net profit in dividend.
- The Credit Lyonnais Securities Europe has recommended buying shares of the Celuloza Swiecie paper mill.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
